subject.title: fix(feishu): pace outbound sends per target

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off Feishu `sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` per-target pacing config contract once the branch is rebased and proven?
rationale: Source inspection shows the missing capability, but adding a durable operator-facing Feishu config key and deciding the acceptable proof/coverage bar requires maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
options.body: Proceed with a rebased PR or replacement that keeps the setting default-off, per-account overridable, and scoped to Feishu-owned send paths with real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep Reactive Retry Only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and document that Feishu delivery relies on existing retry/backoff after rate-limit responses.

options.title: Defer To Broad Rate Limiting
options.body: Pause this PR and let the broader external API rate-limit work define any cross-provider queueing or throttling policy first.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Feishu Pacing
recommendation.body: Proceed with a rebased PR or replacement that keeps the setting default-off, per-account overridable, and scoped to Feishu-owned send paths with real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata names this handle as the community-maintained owner candidate for Feishu-owned behavior.
